component_records.title: Bid qualification, teaming and proposal evidence
component_records.description: The bid is led by a single designated lead organisation that holds the contract and the track allocation, with named subcontractors for outreach, employer engagement and platform hosting disclosed in the proposal. The lead evidences experience in at least three of the four qualifying domains: academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market, with programme histories, cohort counts, cost per participant and placement rates for each. The component assembles the evidence ESD scores: employer commitment letters for paid internships and full-time roles, one-page resumes of key personnel, the annual performance estimates for participants served, low-income completion rate and placement rate, and the current measurement and reporting approach those estimates rest on. It also confirms the entity type and the lead-organisation structure that the teaming arrangement requires. It runs the procurement calendar: all questions are submitted by email to the designated contact by August 29, 2025, the team attends any interview in the first week of November 2025, and the bid is held ready for the November 14, 2025 award announcement so mobilisation can begin on the January 1, 2026 contract start date.

component_records.title: Programme mobilisation and project management office
component_records.description: A programme director and PMO stand up the AI Prep contract on the January 1, 2026 start date, with a monthly plan covering curriculum build, recruitment, cohort delivery and placement through the first cohort's completion. The PMO produces the monthly status reporting and milestone evidence ESD uses to assess whether obligations are performed in a timely and professional manner, and it holds the schedule baseline against which change orders are raised within 30 days of ESD's written notification. It also runs the staff continuity register: named staff are submitted for ESD approval before mobilisation, any proposed change is notified immediately with a summary of the substitute's experience and an interview offered before the substitute starts, and the plan keeps key staff on the project to completion. The PMO maintains the contract change log and continues delivery as modified after any ESD change or addition.

component_records.title: Curriculum design and industry-informed AI training
component_records.description: A curriculum lead and AI faculty build an industry-informed AI curriculum delivered as online courses, with employer input gathered through the partnership workstream so content tracks hiring demand. The curriculum is built for both tracks: Track A gives matriculating undergraduates AI training aimed at paid internships at leading tech companies, and Track B gives an accelerated bootcamp alternative to a degree for New Yorkers with barriers to employment, covering in-demand technical and professional skills. The design fixes an immersive schedule that can run part-time or full-time, states the credentials awarded on completion, and defines skill-attainment assessments at module level. The curriculum is refreshed each cohort against employer feedback and carries real-world machine learning projects with mentor supervision.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment and eligibility assessment
component_records.description: An outreach team runs a targeted recruitment strategy for low-income New Yorkers currently underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own, working through community organisations, public colleges and workforce partners across the state. The component delivers a program application and evaluation process with a scored rubric, income verification and a documented low-income definition applied consistently across both tracks. Every admitted participant completes a needs assessment that records barriers such as childcare, transport, hardware access and prior study, and routes them to the supports they need. Recruitment is sized to enrol at least 250 participants, with a plan and budget that reach more than 400 to earn the priority weighting, and it tracks applicant volume and low-income percentage from first contact.

component_records.title: Participant delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: The administrator delivers and manages the training programme cohort by cohort, with attendance, assessment and progression managed on the platform. Each participant receives a stipend at a published level and wrap-around supports: an assigned mentor, a career coach with industry expertise, and professional development support running through training and into placement. The component also delivers full-time job connection support for Track B participants and paid internship placement support for Track A participants, with placement targets set so the majority of graduates secure a paid internship or full-time AI role. Support spend and stipend levels are budgeted per participant and mapped to the programme duration.

component_records.title: Employer partnership and placement engine
component_records.description: A team of employer partnership managers cultivates and maintains relationships with leading AI employers in New York, both to inform curriculum content and to generate paid internship and full-time job opportunities for graduates. The component secures written employer commitment letters for the proposal and converts them into placement slots per cohort, with a placement pipeline tracked by employer, role and start date. It coordinates directly with individual employers on screening, interview scheduling and onboarding, and it builds the talent pipeline that gives AI employers a repeatable source of low-income New York talent. Placement outcomes are recorded against each graduate so the placement rate can be reported to ESD.

component_records.title: Hosted learning and case-management platform with outcome data
component_records.description: A hosted platform carries the online curriculum, application and assessment workflow, stipend payments, mentor and coach case notes, and the placement pipeline in one system, configured rather than built from scratch. It captures every data point ESD expects: applicant counts and low-income percentage, enrolment counts and low-income percentage, completion counts and low-income percentage, paid internship placement rate and low-income share of placements, full-time job placement rate and low-income share, participating colleges and universities, and participating employer partners. The platform produces a monthly data extract and an on-request export so tracked data can be made available to ESD in whatever cadence and format ESD sets at contract negotiation. Access control, data retention and security configuration are aligned to the ESD IT Security Standard Brief once Appendix A is issued.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost governance
component_records.description: A finance lead builds the line-by-line price proposal: personnel services lines showing job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percentage of time and cost to contract, and separate other-than-personnel-services lines for each item with unit cost and quantity. The budget is built by track and mapped to the programme duration, with staff salary and benefits, wrap-around supports and the participant stipend level as explicit cost categories, plus curriculum development, marketing and events where they are needed for delivery. The budget is capped at $2M for one track and $4M for both, excludes all indirect costs, and states the extent of any cost matching in the ESD budget template. The component also carries the bid cost position that all proposal costs sit with the bidder.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and diversity obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance manager carries the obligations that sit outside programme delivery. The workstream maintains the insurance programme: Commercial General Liability at $1M per occurrence and $2M aggregate, Commercial Automobile at $1M where vehicles are used in business, Sexual Abuse and Molestation cover at $1M, and statutory Workers' Compensation, Employer's Liability and Disability cover, with ESD named as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on general liability and auto and a waiver of subrogation in ESD's favour. It runs the MWBE programme against the 30 percent goal: a Utilization Plan, good faith effort evidence filed through the New York State Contract System, commercially useful function accounting, revised plans for any post-award change, and quarterly compliance and payment reporting. It runs the SDVOB programme against the 6 percent goal: the OCSD-4 Utilization Plan, good faith effort evidence including solicitations and responses, written remedies within seven business days of any notice of deficiency, waiver requests on OCSD-5 within five business days where directed, and monthly SDVOB compliance reporting. It certifies compliance with the New York State Human Rights Law and the non-discrimination and equal employment obligations, and maintains the periodic State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k disclosures and ST-220-CA certifications through the term. It holds the responsibility position: financial ability, organisational capacity and legal authority evidenced in the Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire, satisfactory performance of prior government contracts, and acceptance of the contract clauses that keep the contractor responsible and allow ESD to suspend or terminate on a non-responsibility finding. It manages the conduct rules: no contact with State employees outside the designated contacts, no gifts, no employment offers to involved ESD staff for 30 days after their involvement closes, conflict of interest disclosure and mitigation, and disclosure of any Commission on Ethics and Lobbying investigation. It secures ESD approval for any subcontractor not named in the proposal, confirms every worker's qualifications, licences and right to work, and confirms no assignment of the agreement. It accepts Schedule A and Schedule B, warrants services to professional standards, corrects patent errors at no charge, and files any debriefing request within 15 calendar days of a non-selection notice.

items.text: Budget cap of $2M per track may not cover 400 participants with stipends and supports. ESD caps the award at $2M per track and $4M for both, and bars indirect costs, but the RFP gives no participant volume, cohort size or stipend level. The proposed solution assumes 400 participants at a $5,000 stipend, which alone is $2M across both tracks before curriculum, staff, mentors, coaches, platform and placement work. If that assumption is wrong the programme is either loss-making or under-delivers on the participant count that earns priority. The stipend assumption consumes the entire combined ceiling before any delivery cost, and indirect costs are unallowable so overhead cannot be recovered. The RFP settles neither participant volume nor stipend level.

The proposal must include letters from partner employers committing to paid internships or full-time roles, and the majority of graduates must be placed. items.text: Eighteen-month term and January 2026 start leave no room for a late award or Comptroller approval. The award may also require Office of the State Comptroller approval before it is enforceable. A delayed award or approval compresses mobilisation, curriculum build and recruitment into the same window and puts the first-cohort placement date at risk. The solution's schedule assumes a firm January 1, 2026 start, while the RFP reserves the right to change dates and the contract is not enforceable until Comptroller approval.

items.text: Email and Dropbox submission rules conflict and a single misstep voids the bid. One requirement says all contacts and inquiries go by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov, another says email submissions will not be accepted and proposals must go only to the designated Dropbox, and late proposals are rejected outright. The proposed solution plans questions by email and a Dropbox submission. If the team sends the proposal or a clarification to the wrong channel, the bid is disqualified on a technicality. The conflict is real but the correct reading is clear enough, and the consequence of getting it wrong is outright rejection rather than rework.

items.text: Low-income and barriers-to-employment definitions are undefined, driving recruitment cost. The RFP requires over 50 percent low-income participants and targets New Yorkers with barriers to employment but never defines either term. The proposed solution invents a 200 percent federal poverty level or Pell eligibility test. If ESD applies a narrower definition, recruitment volume and verification effort rise sharply and the low-income percentage and completion metrics may be missed. Eligibility definitions determine recruitment reach, verification cost and the reported low-income percentages, and the RFP leaves them open while the solution fixes its own definition as an inference.
items.reason: Over 50% low-income and the request that respondents define it are supported; the claim that barriers to employment is undefined is not shown.

items.text: Bidding both tracks under one lead organisation strains capacity and the $4M ceiling. The proposed solution bids both tracks under a single lead organisation with one combined $4M ceiling, although ESD may award up to two administrators. Running two tracks simultaneously needs separate recruitment, curriculum and placement capacity, and the RFP asks for a specific description of how a respondent will manage both. If the combined bid is weaker than two focused bids, or if ESD awards the tracks to different administrators, the pricing and staffing model breaks. The RFP does not say whether a bidder may bid one track or must bid both, and the solution's single-award assumption is an inference that shapes the whole price and staffing plan.
items.reason: Up to two administrators, lead organisation and dual-track description supported; the 'RFP does not say' bid-one-or-both claim contradicted by 'Track A and/or Track B'.

items.text: Thirty percent MWBE and six percent SDVOB goals must be met from a thin subcontractor base. The contract carries a 30 percent MWBE and 6 percent SDVOB participation goal, with utilisation plans, good faith effort evidence, quarterly and monthly compliance reporting, and breach consequences for willful failure. The proposed solution subcontracts outreach, employer engagement and platform hosting, so certified firms must be found for a meaningful share of that spend. If certified subcontractors cannot be identified, the bid risks a deficient utilisation plan and withheld payments. The goals are firm and the reporting obligations are detailed, but the RFP does not supply the MWBE directory or the OCSD forms, and the solution's subcontracting scope is limited.
items.reason: Goals, plans, reporting and breach supported; claim RFP doesn't supply MWBE directory or OCSD forms contradicted by directory links.

items.text: Insurance coverages and waiver of subrogation are assumed applicable and may be mispriced. The proposed solution prices all of them and assumes the waiver on every policy. If Sexual Abuse and Molestation cover is unavailable or the waiver cannot be obtained on Workers' Compensation, the bid is either overpriced or non-compliant at contract signature. The RFP does not say which coverages apply to a training services contract, and the solution's assumption that all apply and that every policy carries the waiver is an inference that affects price and insurability.

The proposed solution names a programme director, curriculum lead, faculty, partnership managers, coaches and a compliance manager. If a named person leaves, the replacement process can stall delivery and the proposal's staffing evidence weakens. The approval and substitution process is mandatory and the solution depends on a small named team over an 18-month term, so a departure is plausible and the approval step adds delay.
